issues.body: After seeing `prefix:`, the scanner consumes only ASCII alphanumeric, `_`, `-`, and `.`. SPARQL PN_LOCAL also permits Unicode name characters, percent escapes, and backslash-escaped PN_LOCAL_ESC characters. For an input containing a valid term such as `ex:éFLTR` or an escaped local-name character followed by `FLTR`, scanning stops inside the prefixed name; subsequent ASCII text is then treated as a bare word and may yield `FLTR -> FILTER` when some unrelated syntax error causes the canary to fail. This contradicts the public guarantee that prefixed-name local parts are data and never keyword candidates, and makes the principal precision invariant inadequately enforced.
issues.fix_hint: Skip a complete SPARQL prefixed-name/blank-node token using the grammar's PN_LOCAL character and escape rules (or reuse an existing lexer) rather than the current ASCII approximation. Add integration regressions that trigger an unrelated parse failure while valid Unicode, percent-escaped, and backslash-escaped prefixed names contain typo-shaped ASCII suffixes, asserting that no suggestion is emitted.
issues.title: Valid prefixed-name suffixes can be misclassified as keyword typos

verdict.summary: The diagnostic is fail-closed and does not rewrite the query, but its scanner does not actually exclude every prefixed-name local part as claimed. Valid SPARQL prefixed names can contain characters outside the small ASCII set consumed after `:`, so an ASCII suffix inside the same RDF term can be rescanned as a bare word and produce a misleading keyword suggestion. The tests cover only simple local names and do not exercise the load-bearing lexical-boundary claim.
